To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a shared buffer with a threshold priority scheme provides significant improvements over a comparable switch with a fixed buffer and no priority scheme, and that such improvements can be achieved without a large increase in switch complexity or cost.

the use of a threshold priority mechanism in an ATM switch can improve both cell loss probability and resource utilization, and that the performance improvement is more pronounced for stringent loss requirements.
the partial buffer sharing mechanism is effective in improving the performance of a shared-buffer ATM switching element and that its implementation is not overly complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a switch design which is both loss sensitive and delay sensitive.
the performance evaluation and optimal dimensioning of an ATM switching system with threshold priority.
the development of an approximate analysis method and its use in the dimensioning of a switch with a threshold priority scheme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the partial buffer sharing mechanism is a very effective means for achieving a desired level of loss performance, with a relatively small increase in buffer requirements.
a partial buffer sharing switch with threshold priority is a very promising design.
the partial buffer sharing mechanism is a very attractive alternative to the conventional buffer sharing mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the partial buffer sharing mechanism, when appropriately dimensioned, is a viable means of improving the performance of an ATM switch.
the use of threshold priority is a very attractive option in the design of an ATM switching element.
the threshold priority mechanism is a viable and attractive alternative to other priority mechanisms for ATM switching elements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with a modest amount of additional hardware, the performance of an ATM switch can be significantly improved, especially in terms of loss probability.
a partial buffer sharing mechanism is an effective means to provide a desired level of loss differentiation between cell types in a shared buffer switch.
, with a threshold priority scheme, the switch can be made much more efficient, in terms of both loss and delay performance, than without such a scheme.
